capitals.name: Almaliq
capitals.note: Chagatai Khan page: 'Almaliq was his capital and summer pastures'; the Chagatai Khanate infobox lists Almaliq and Qarshi (Qarshi 65.8 E, 38.87 N). Alghu was buried at Almaliq; Ariq Boke held it 1263-64. Ends 1266 (repair of 2026-10-19): after the peace of c.1267 the Ili and Almaliq are Kaidu's in fact (ogedeid-ulus gains Almaliq in 1277). The Alghu and Duwa pages name no seat for 1267-1293, so none is given; Qarshi is on the Chagatai Khanate infobox without a date.

rulers.name: Qara Hülegü (Ebuskun regent)
rulers.note: Too young to rule; the widowed khatun Ebuskun was regent. Replaced by Güyük in 1246.

rulers.name: Yesü Möngke
rulers.note: Installed by Güyük in 1246; deposed by Möngke in 1252, who installed Qara Hülegü again.

rulers.name: Mubarak Shah (Orghana regent)
rulers.note: Qara Hülegü died on the way home and his young son Mubarak Shah succeeded under his mother Orghana; the page gives no year for the accession; Ariq Boke replaced him in 1260.

rulers.name: Mubarak Shah (second reign)
rulers.note: Orghana placed him on the throne once again after Alghu's death in 1265; Baraq deposed him in September 1266 (Baraq page).

rulers.name: Baraq
rulers.note: Reign 1266 to 9 August 1271; repudiated Kublai; 'accepted peace with Kaidu' c.1267.

rulers.name: Negübei
rulers.note: Enthroned by Kaidu; the Kaidu page has him murdered by Buqa Temür in 1272, the Chagatai page has him replaced in 1274.

rulers.name: Buqa Temür
rulers.note: Replaced Negübei in 1274 (Chagatai page); his death date is uncertain; Kaidu appointed Duwa in 1282 (Duwa page).

rulers.name: Duwa
rulers.note: Duwa reigned 1282-1307 (Duwa page infobox); the ulus becomes the Chagatai Khanate row in 1294.

1264: the Ili is free again. Ariq Böke 'traveled to Shangdu alone and surrendered to Kublai in 1264, ending the civil war' (Toluid page); Alghu returned to the Ili and died there in 1265 (buried at Almaliq).

The Golden Horde page says only 'A 1267 peace gave one-third of Transoxiana to Kaidu and Mengu-Timur' and that 'the left bank of Khorazm would eventually be retaken'; the Mengu-Timur page is silent on both regions. The ogedeid-ulus dossier begins only with Kaidu's investiture at Talas in August/September 1271, so this dossier keeps the land until then, so that no year draws it for no state; the de facto hand-over was 1267-1269 (repair of 2026-10-19, at the reviewer's request).

wars.name: Toluid Civil War (Chagatai front)

zones.text: the Ili valley, lost by Alghu to Ariq Böke

wars.outcome: Kublai won. Alghu, Ariq's appointee, turned on Ariq in 1262-63; Ariq took Almalikh and Alghu fled to Samarkand in 1263; Ariq surrendered at Shangdu in 1264; Alghu died in 1265.

wars.name: Baraq–Kaidu war

zones.text: the east of Transoxania and the Bukhara region

wars.outcome: Kaidu, helped by Möngke-Temür's Golden Horde army, beat Baraq near Khujand; Baraq kept two thirds of Transoxiana and gave up the east and the Bukhara region at the peace of c.1267 (or 1269). The dossier hands the land over in 1271, the year of Kaidu's investiture and of the ogedeid-ulus dossier.
wars.note: Dating: Chagatai page and the Baraq page's Wassaf date put the peace in 1267; the Kaidu page has the war in 1268 and the peace c.1267 or spring 1269 (Rashid al-Din).

wars.name: Baraq’s invasion of the Ilkhanate
wars.outcome: Baraq beat the governor Buchin in Khorasan, then lost to Abaqa near Herat on 22 July 1270 and retreated to Bukhara; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Ilkhanid invasion of Transoxiana
wars.outcome: Abaqa 'invaded Transoxania in 1272 and sacked Bukhara, carrying off 50,000 captives' (Chagatai page); a raid, no land changed hands.

wars.name: Kaidu–Kublai war (Chagatai side)

zones.text: the Tarim Basin, garrisoned by the Yuan at Khotan (1276) and Beshbalik (1278) until 1288/89

wars.outcome: 'In 1275, Duwa joined Kaidu in the war against the Yuan dynasty but were repelled' (Chagatai page); the Yuan left the Tarim in 1288/89.

certainty.note: Steppe, oasis and mountain frontiers throughout; no treaty line is recorded. The peace of c.1267 divides Transoxiana by thirds, not by a surveyed line.

notes:
The Chagatai ulus before Cliopatria's 1294 Chagatai Khanate row: no Cliopatria shape exists, so all three keyframes are new and drawn from pages that name regions, not boundaries. The ulus is inside Cliopatria's Mongol Empire row throughout (1206-1293); the rendering agents should draw it over that row.

Dating disagreements: the peace between Baraq and Kaidu is 1267 (Chagatai page), c.1267 or spring 1269 (Kaidu and Baraq pages); Negübei's end is 1272 (Kaidu page) or 1274 (Chagatai page); Alghu's death 1265 or 1266 (Alghu page). Independence from the Mongol Empire: the Chagatai infobox 'Administrative region of the Mongol Empire (1227-1266)', independent from 1266, but no territorial event marks it (Baraq repudiated Kublai in 1266; Kublai's nominal suzerainty was acknowledged again in 1303).

Not drawn because the pages opened do not locate it: Alghu's gains of Samarkand, Bukhara and 'lands formerly held by the Blue Horde' after 1261 (Alghu page, undated); the imperial governors of Transoxiana (Mahmud Yalavach, then Mas'ud Beg) who ran the cities. The Alghu page says 'Blue Horde' where it means Berke's Golden Horde (Cliopatria's Blue Horde row is 1363-1449). The 1263 Ili devastation is on the Chagatai page; the Toluid page has Alghu losing Almalikh to Ariq. 

Counterparts needing entries in other dossiers: mongol-empire (1227 hand-over; its ledger covers the whole empire), yuan-dynasty (Tarim contest 1266-1289; Khotan garrison 1276, Beshbalik 1278), ilkhanate (the 1270 Herat war), ariq-boke (Ili occupation 1263-64), ogedeid-ulus (the 1267 loss), golden-horde (Möngke-Temür's army against Baraq).
 [Reviewer ia-02-x, 2026-10-19] Pre-1294 counterparts and belligerents changed to the slugs alive in those years: yuan-dynasty to mongol-empire, ilkhanate to ulus-of-hulegu, golden-horde to ulus-of-jochi (the Cliopatria rows of the three successors start in 1294).

[Repair ia-02-x, 2026-10-19] Reviewer findings applied: (1) vassal_start 1260 / vassal_end 1262 with ariq-boke (Alghu page). (2) vassal_start 1271 with ogedeid-ulus (Duwa page: subservience 'since 1271') and vassal_end 1293 (c1, bookkeeping).
